newsitem.title: USA: Strike shuts IBP cattle plant in Illinois.
newsitem.headline: Strike shuts IBP cattle plant in Illinois.

text.p: A strike has shut down IBP Inc's cattle slaughter and processing plant in Joslin, Ill., after workers rejected a new contract proposal on Saturday, a company official said.
"My understanding is, there were about 35 picketers this morning at two different plant entrances," said Gary Mickelson, IBP company spokesman.
Mickelson said the work stoppage took effect at 0101 CST (0701 GMT) on Tuesday and involved about 1,800 members of the United Food and Commercial Workers Union (UFCW) local 1540.
The plant slaughters 2,000 to 3,000 cattle per day, industry sources estimated.
"We have begun the process of increasing production at some of our other plants to offset the (production) loss of Joslin," Mickelson said.
IBP's beef plants typically do not run at full production this time of year, so there was more than enough available capacity to make up for the shutdown at Joslin, he said.
Mickelson said the company was in contact with a federal mediator and was willing to sit down and meet with the union, but no meeting date had been set.
Union officials were not available for comment.

The previous UFCW contract at the plant expired on October 20. Union officials on Monday said IBP's new wage offers had been acceptable but company proposals to scale back insurance coverage and profit-sharing were not.
